subject: Cognitive Science
title: Situated Cognition
description: A short lesson to help you apply Situated Cognition.

hook.text: Brazilian street vendors do complex math selling produce but fail the same math on a paper test.

buildup.text: Situated cognition says knowledge is bound to the context where it was learned and used.

discovery.text: Jean Lave showed that math ability isn't general—it's tied to the activity and environment.

twist.text: This challenges classroom education: skills learned at a desk may not transfer to real life.

climax.text: Effective learning happens in authentic contexts, not in isolated drills disconnected from use.

quiz.question: What does situated cognition claim about knowledge?
options: It is tied to the context where it was learned
It transfers easily to any setting

details.summary: Situated cognition argues that learning is inseparable from the context in which it occurs. Knowledge is not abstract content transferred from teacher to student but is constructed through activity in authentic situations.
details.whyItMatters: Situated cognition explains the transfer problem: why students who pass exams cannot apply knowledge in practice. Learning in authentic contexts produces more usable knowledge.
takeaways: Learning is tied to the context and activity in which it occurs
Abstract knowledge often fails to transfer to real situations
Authentic tasks and contexts produce more usable knowledge

faq.question: Why does classroom learning often fail to transfer?
faq.answer: Classroom problems are cleaned and simplified, with clear boundaries and known methods. Real-world problems are messy, ill-defined, and require knowledge from multiple domains. Knowledge learned out of context becomes inert information that students can recite but cannot apply flexibly.

faq.question: How can instruction be more situated?
faq.answer: Use real-world problems, case studies, simulations, and project-based learning. Have students work in authentic contexts or with realistic constraints. Apprenticeship models, internships, and problem-based learning all embody situated cognition principles.
